items.stem: A study in Singapore recorded hours of revision (x) and test score (%) (y): (1, 30), (3, 33), (5, 55), (6, 66), (7, 55), (11, 80), (12, 80), (13, 97). Describe the correlation shown on a scatter diagram and interpret it in context.
items.answer: strong positive correlation
items.markingKey: strong positive correlation (A1 A1: direction and strength); interpretation – as hours of revision increases, test score (%) tends to increase (R1).

items.stem: Which interval represents −9 < x < −3?
items.markingKey: B. Round bracket at −9 (excluded); round bracket at −3: (−9, −3).

items.stem: The depth of water at a jetty is D = 5 cos(15t) + 14 metres, t hours after midnight. (a) Find D at t = 18. (b) For how long in each 24-hour cycle is the depth more than 15.8 m?
items.answer: (a) 14.0 m (b) about 9.2 hours
items.markingKey: Substitution (A1); solve D = 15.8 for the boundary times (M1 A1); duration (A1).

items.stem: In general, f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) are:
items.answer: different
items.markingKey: different. The order of composition matters.

items.stem: A delivery van bought in Melbourne for A$45,000 depreciates by 10% per year. After how many whole years is it first worth half its original value or less?
items.answer: 7 years

items.stem: How many real roots has x² + 7x − 5 = 0?
items.answer: two distinct real roots

items.stem: In triangle ABC, a = 11 cm, b = 13.2 cm and A = 53°. Find the possible values of angle B, to 1 d.p.
Which formula gives the n-th term of an arithmetic sequence?
items.answer: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d
items.markingKey: uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d. Start at u₁ and add d a total of n − 1 times.

items.stem: Boat A starts at (13 over −3) with velocity (−3 over 4) and boat B starts at (13 over 9) with velocity (−3 over −2) (km and km/h). Show that they collide and find when and where.
items.answer: t = 2 h at (7 over 5)
items.markingKey: Positions r₀ + tv for both (M1); equate both components (M1); same t from both equations (R1); t and point (A1).

items.stem: Which value is excluded from the domain of f(x) = 5/(x + 2)?
items.markingKey: x = −2. Division by zero is undefined.

items.stem: A vector has magnitude 15 and makes an angle of 105° anticlockwise with the positive x-axis. Write it as a column vector with components to 3 s.f.
Find the sum of the first 5 terms of 1, 3, 9, 27, ….
Kwame says that for h = 25t − 5t² the ball is highest at t = 5. Explain the mistake and correct it.
items.answer: t = 5 is when it lands (h = 0). The highest point is midway between the roots: t = 2.5, h = 31.2 m.
items.markingKey: Mistake identified (R1); correct maximum (A1).

items.stem: "−2(3 over 1) = (−6 over 1)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Every component is multiplied: (−6 over −2).
items.markingKey: Every component is multiplied: (−6 over −2). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Without a calculator, explain which is larger: 3√6 or 3√5.
items.markingKey: Both written as single roots (M1); comparison justified (R1).

items.stem: Ingrid writes log 18 ÷ log 6 = log 3. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: Division of logs is not a log law; log(18/6) = log 18 − log 6 = log 3. log 18 ÷ log 6 ≈ 1.61 is log₆ 18.
items.markingKey: Correct law (R1); value check (A1).

items.stem: A charity in Geneva starts a message chain: in round 1 one person sends it to 3 people, and in every later round each new receiver sends it to 3 more. (a) Write the number of new receivers in rounds 1, 2 and 3. (b) Write an expression for round n. (c) Without a calculator, find the round in which 243 new people receive it. (d) Find the total number of receivers in the first 5 rounds.
items.markingKey: (a) 3, 9, 27 (b) 3^n (c) 3^n = 243 = 3⁵, so n = 5 rounds (d) total = 3(3⁵ − 1)/(3 − 1) = 363. Model or common base set up (M1); exponents equated and solved (A1 A1); pattern generalised (B: R1); interpretation in context (D: R1).

items.stem: Explain why one very large value affects the standard deviation more than it affects the interquartile range.
items.answer: σ uses the squared distance of every value from the mean, so an extreme value adds a large squared term; the IQR uses only the middle 50%.
items.markingKey: Squared deviation (R1); IQR ignores extremes (R1).

items.stem: A forest near Accra covers 5,000 km² and is shrinking by 5% per year. (a) Write a model for the area A after t years. (b) Find the area after 10 years. (c) After how many whole years will half of the forest be gone? (d) Suggest a reason why the model might change.
items.answer: (a) A = 5000 × 0.95ᵗ km² (b) 2,994 km² (c) 14 years (d) e.g. replanting would change the multiplier; deforestation rates vary
items.markingKey: (a) A = 5000 × 0.95ᵗ km² (b) 2,994 km² (c) 14 years (d) e.g. replanting would change the multiplier; deforestation rates vary. Correct exponential model (A1 M1); calculations (A1 A1); interpretation and limitations (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: f(x) = x² − 6x. Find y = −f(x) in simplified form and describe the transformation.
items.answer: y = −x² + 6x; reflection in the x-axis
items.markingKey: Every term negated (M1); −x² + 6x (A1); reflection in the x-axis (A1).

items.stem: A student project in Hanoi collected outside temperature (°C) (x) and heating bill (y) for 10 cases: (2, 151), (4, 126), (5, 46), (6, 173), (8, 74), (9, 103), (16, 117), (19, 124), (22, 86), (24, 21). (a) Identify the independent and dependent variables. (b) Describe the correlation. (c) Interpret it in context. (d) Explain one reason why you cannot conclude that x causes y.
items.answer: (a) independent: outside temperature (°C); dependent: heating bill (b) weak negative correlation (r ≈ −0.45) (c) as outside temperature (°C) increases, heating bill tends to decrease (d) e.g. a lurking variable or a small sample of 10 – the data show association, not proof of cause
items.markingKey: (a) independent: outside temperature (°C); dependent: heating bill (b) weak negative correlation (r ≈ −0.45) (c) as outside temperature (°C) increases, heating bill tends to decrease (d) e.g. a lurking variable or a small sample of 10 – the data show association, not proof of cause. Variables (A1); correlation described with direction and strength (A1 A1); interpretation (C1); critical reflection (D: R1).

items.stem: An exponential model y = a × bˣ passes through (2, 45/2) and (5, 1215/16). Find a and b.

Investigate y = kx² for k = 2, 3, 4. (a) Find the point with x = 1 on each. (b) Describe each as a transformation of y = x². (c) Show that y = kx² can also be described as a horizontal stretch. (d) Find the horizontal scale factor for k = 5.
items.answer: (a) the points (1, k) are (1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4) (b) each is a vertical stretch of y = x² with factor k (c) kx² = (√k x)², so it is also a horizontal stretch with factor 1/√k (d) for k = 5: factor 1/√5 ≈ 0.447
items.markingKey: (a) the points (1, k) are (1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4) (b) each is a vertical stretch of y = x² with factor k (c) kx² = (√k x)², so it is also a horizontal stretch with factor 1/√k (d) for k = 5: factor 1/√5 ≈ 0.447. Stretch identified with correct factor (A1 A1); function written (A1); interpreted / generalised (B/D: R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = 2x − 1 meets the curve y = 2x² + 6x − 1.
items.markingKey: 2x² + 6x − 1 = 2x − 1 → 2x² + 4x = 0 (M1); x = −2, 0 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: From a coastguard station near Cape Town, boat A is 31 km away on a bearing of 040° and boat B is 37 km away on a bearing of 130°. (a) Find the angle AOB at the station. (b) Find the distance AB. (c) Find the bearing of B from A. (d) How long would A take to reach B at 30 km/h?
items.answer: (a) 90° (b) 48.3 km (c) 170° (d) 96.5 minutes at 30 km/h
items.markingKey: (a) 90° (b) 48.3 km (c) 170° (d) 96.5 minutes at 30 km/h. Diagram / angles correctly identified (A1); sine or cosine rule and Pythagoras applied (M1 A1); bearings in three-figure form (C1); interpretation (D: R1).

items.stem: "A′ ∩ B′ means 'not in A and B'." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It means in neither A nor B: (A ∪ B)′.
items.markingKey: It means in neither A nor B: (A ∪ B)′. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "combined transformation"?
options: The transformation y = a f(x), which multiplies every y-value by a; scale factor a parallel to the y-axis
Two or more transformations applied in sequence, e.g. y = a f(x − h) + k
The transformation y = f(x) + k, which moves the graph k units up (down if k < 0)
The transformation y = f(−x): every x-value changes sign; (x, y) → (−x, y)
items.answer: Two or more transformations applied in sequence, e.g. y = a f(x − h) + k
items.markingKey: B. "combined transformation" is two or more transformations applied in sequence, e.g. y = a f(x − h) + k.

items.stem: Without a calculator, state the two consecutive integers between which log₃ 723 lies. Then use a calculator to evaluate it to 3 s.f.
Two triangles with sides 6, 9 and included angles 40° and 140° have:
items.answer: equal areas
items.markingKey: equal areas. sin 40° = sin 140°.

items.stem: Data for hours of revision (x) and test score (%) (y): (2, 38), (5, 52), (8, 0), (10, 69), (11, 78), (13, 88), (14, 87), (15, 98). (a) Identify the outlier. (b) Calculate r with and without it, to 3 d.p. (c) Comment on its effect.
items.answer: (a) (8, 0) (b) with: 0.722; without: 0.992 (c) the outlier weakens the correlation
items.markingKey: Outlier (A1); both r values from GDC (A1 A1); comment (R1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A way of writing a set of real numbers between two endpoints, using [ ] for included endpoints and ( ) for excluded ones, e.g. (−2, 5]"?
items.answer: interval notation
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of interval notation.

items.stem: Use vectors to determine whether A(6, 3), B(7, −1) and C(8, −5) are collinear.
items.answer: AB = (1 over −4), AC = (2 over −8); AC = 2 AB, so collinear
items.markingKey: AB and AC found (A1 A1); scalar multiple tested with a common point (R1); conclusion (A1).

items.stem: In a cuboid, the space diagonal is found by:
items.answer: Pythagoras twice
items.markingKey: Pythagoras twice. Base diagonal first, then the space diagonal.

items.stem: The graph of y = √x is translated to give y = √(x + 2). Describe the translation and find the image of the end point (0, 0).
items.answer: translation (−2 over 0); (−2, 0)
items.markingKey: Vector (A1); image point (−2, 0) (A1).

items.stem: Solve 1.5ˣ = 10, to 3 s.f.
A student claims: "Decay by 20% per year means N = N₀ × 0.2ᵗ." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Keeping 80% each year gives N₀ × 0.8ᵗ.
items.markingKey: Keeping 80% each year gives N₀ × 0.8ᵗ. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Define the term "loan".
items.answer: Money borrowed that must be repaid with interest, usually in regular instalments
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: money borrowed that must be repaid with interest, usually in regular instalments. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Priya says 5 people can sit in a row of 5 chairs in 5 × 5 = 25 ways. Explain the error.
items.answer: Once a person is seated they cannot be chosen again: 5 × 4 × … × 1 = 5! = 120.
items.markingKey: Choices decrease (R1); value (A1).

items.stem: "A graph can never cross any asymptote." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It never meets a vertical asymptote, but it may cross a horizontal one for small x.
items.markingKey: It never meets a vertical asymptote, but it may cross a horizontal one for small x. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why y = (1/3)ˣ and y = 3^(−x) are the same graph.
items.answer: (1/3)ˣ = 3^(−x) by the laws of exponents: both are the reflection of y = 3ˣ in the y-axis.
items.markingKey: Index law (R1); reflection (R1).

items.stem: "A line of best fit must go through the first and last points." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It follows the overall trend, passing through the mean point, not particular points.
items.markingKey: It follows the overall trend, passing through the mean point, not particular points. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A pizzeria in Kuala Lumpur cuts a pizza of radius 23 cm into 10 equal slices and sells the pizza for RM18. (a) Find the angle of each slice in radians. (b) Find the area of a slice. (c) Find the length of crust on a slice. (d) Find the price per slice and per 100 cm².
items.answer: (a) 2π/10 ≈ 0.628 rad (b) 166 cm² (c) crust 14.5 cm (d) RM1.80 per slice; RM1.08 per 100 cm²
items.markingKey: (a) 2π/10 ≈ 0.628 rad (b) 166 cm² (c) crust 14.5 cm (d) RM1.80 per slice; RM1.08 per 100 cm². Radians used (A1); arc / sector formulas (M1 A1 A1); interpreted in context (D: R1).

items.stem: Tomás solves x² = 5x by dividing by x and gets x = 5. Explain what is wrong and give the full solution.
items.answer: Dividing by x loses the root x = 0. x² − 5x = 0 → x(x − 5) = 0 → x = 0 or x = 5.
items.markingKey: Lost root explained (R1); both roots (A1).

items.stem: A Ferris wheel in Singapore has radius 25 m with its hub 30 m above the ground. A cabin is at 210° anticlockwise from the horizontal through the hub. (a) Find its coordinates relative to the hub. (b) Find its height relative to the hub. (c) Find its height above the ground. (d) Find another angle at which a cabin is at the same height.
items.answer: (a) (−21.7, −12.5) m (b) height above the hub −12.5 m (c) 17.5 m above the ground (d) another angle with the same height: 330°
items.markingKey: (a) (−21.7, −12.5) m (b) height above the hub −12.5 m (c) 17.5 m above the ground (d) another angle with the same height: 330°. Unit-circle values (A1 A1); quadrant / sign reasoning (R1); pattern or context (B/D: R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: A survey about school lunches in Lisbon is sent by email and only 12% reply. Identify the source of bias and suggest an improvement.
items.answer: Non-response bias: those who reply may have strong opinions. Improvement: Follow up non-responders or use a smaller random sample with interviews.
items.markingKey: Bias identified and explained (R1 A1); sensible improvement (A1).

items.stem: A mobile plan in Kuala Lumpur costs RM10 per month plus RM3 per GB, with a cap of 20 GB. (a) Write the cost C as a function of the data used, g GB. (b) State a suitable domain. (c) Find the range. (d) Explain how the domain changes if data is charged only in whole GB.
items.answer: (a) C(g) = 10 + 3g (b) 0 ≤ g ≤ 20 (c) RM10 ≤ C ≤ RM70 (d) a discrete domain if only whole GB are charged: g ∈ {0, 1, …, 20}
items.markingKey: (a) C(g) = 10 + 3g (b) 0 ≤ g ≤ 20 (c) RM10 ≤ C ≤ RM70 (d) a discrete domain if only whole GB are charged: g ∈ {0, 1, …, 20}. Function modelled (A1); domain justified from context (R1 A1); range found (A1); communication with correct notation (C1).

items.stem: Using the table – Grade 9: football 4, swimming 19, dance 6; Grade 10: football 7, swimming 28, dance 5 – determine whether choosing dance is independent of being in the group "Grade 9".
items.answer: P(dance) = 11/69 ≈ 0.159; P(dance | Grade 9) = 6/29 ≈ 0.207; not independent
items.markingKey: Both probabilities (A1 A1); comparison and conclusion (R1).

items.stem: A yacht near Halifax starts at (−3 over 2) km relative to a lighthouse at the origin and sails with velocity (1 over −2) km/h. (a) Write its position at time t. (b) Write the square of its distance from the lighthouse. (c) Find when it is closest to the lighthouse. (d) Find the closest distance.
items.answer: (a) r = (−3 over 2) + t(1 over −2) (b) |r|² = (t − 3)² + (−2t + 2)² (c) minimum at t ≈ 1.40 h (d) closest distance ≈ 1.79 km
items.markingKey: (a) r = (−3 over 2) + t(1 over −2) (b) |r|² = (t − 3)² + (−2t + 2)² (c) minimum at t ≈ 1.40 h (d) closest distance ≈ 1.79 km. Velocity / position vectors modelled (M1 A1); calculations (A1 A1); interpreted in context (D: R1).

items.stem: A parabola has vertex (3, 4) and passes through (1, −4). Find its equation in vertex form.

A student in Vienna records the daily views (hundreds) of a video at t = 0 to 5 days: 299, 258, 218, 183, 157, 134. (a) Investigate whether an exponential model is suitable. (b) Find a model y = a × bᵗ using the first value and the mean ratio. (c) Compare the model with the data at t = 3. (d) Use the model to predict t = 9 and comment on its reliability.
items.answer: (a) ratios 0.863, 0.845, 0.839, 0.858, 0.854 – roughly constant, so exponential (b) y ≈ 299 × 0.852ᵗ (c) t = 3: 185 vs 183 (residual −1.9) (d) 70.7; extrapolation – the value levels off / measurement error grows
items.markingKey: (a) ratios 0.863, 0.845, 0.839, 0.858, 0.854 – roughly constant, so exponential (b) y ≈ 299 × 0.852ᵗ (c) t = 3: 185 vs 183 (residual −1.9) (d) 70.7; extrapolation – the value levels off / measurement error grows. Ratios used to justify the model (B: M1 R1); model parameters (A1 A1); residual / prediction and reliability (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: A rectangular garden in Toronto has perimeter 50 m. Write the area in terms of the width x and find the maximum area.
items.answer: A = x(25 − x); max 156 m² when x = 12.5 m
items.markingKey: Length = 25 − x (A1); A = x(25 − x) (M1); vertex x = 12.5 (A1); 156 m² (A1).

items.stem: A quantity starts at 200 and decreases by 3% per year. Which model gives N after t years?
items.markingKey: A. Multiplier 0.97.

items.stem: f(x) = (x − 5)² − 4 for x ≥ 5. Find f⁻¹(x), and state its domain and range.
items.answer: f⁻¹(x) = 5 + √(x + 4); domain x ≥ −4; range f⁻¹(x) ≥ 5
items.markingKey: x = (y − 5)² − 4 (M1); positive root since y ≥ 5 (R1); f⁻¹(x) = 5 + √(x + 4) (A1); domain/range swap (A1).

items.stem: r = −0.7 describes:
items.answer: moderate to strong negative correlation
items.markingKey: A. Negative sign, |r| = 0.7.

items.stem: Solve sin 3x = −0.3 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, giving answers to 1 d.p. where necessary.
items.markingKey: Let u = 3x, 0° ≤ u ≤ 1080° (M1); u-values (A1); divide by 3 (A1); all 6 solutions (A1).

items.stem: Find the exact value of cos 240°.
items.markingKey: C. Related angle 60°; sign from the quadrant.

items.stem: Rationalise the denominator: 6/(5 + √7).
items.markingKey: Multiply by the conjugate (5 − √7) (M1); denominator 25 − 7 = 18 (A1); (5 − √7)/3 (A1).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "line of best fit"?
options: A straight line that best represents the trend of the points on a scatter diagram
Predicting a value within the range of the data – usually reliable when the correlation is strong
The value r², the proportion of the variation in y explained by the linear model
The case r = 1 or r = −1: all points lie exactly on a straight line
items.answer: A straight line that best represents the trend of the points on a scatter diagram
items.markingKey: A. "line of best fit" is a straight line that best represents the trend of the points on a scatter diagram.

items.stem: "The sine rule only works in right-angled triangles." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It works in any triangle; SOHCAHTOA is the special right-angled case.
items.markingKey: It works in any triangle; SOHCAHTOA is the special right-angled case. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Simplify log 4 + log 25.
n(U) = 28, n(A) = 15, n(B) = 19 and n(A ∪ B)′ = 1. Find n(A ∩ B) and P(A ∩ B′).
Which of the following best describes "independent variable"?
options: Data with two variables measured for each item, which can be plotted as points (x, y)
A straight line that best represents the trend of the points on a scatter diagram
The variable that is controlled or chosen, plotted on the horizontal axis
Predicting a value outside the range of the data – often unreliable
items.answer: The variable that is controlled or chosen, plotted on the horizontal axis
items.markingKey: C. "independent variable" is the variable that is controlled or chosen, plotted on the horizontal axis.

items.stem: A car drives at 66 km/h. Explain whether this is a speed or a velocity, and what extra information would make it the other.
items.answer: 66 km/h has no direction, so it is a speed (scalar); adding a direction, e.g. "66 km/h due north", makes it a velocity.
items.markingKey: Classification (A1); direction needed (R1).

items.stem: The daily temperatures (°C) recorded in Vienna were: 22, 7, 39, 9, 5, 32, 40, 8. Use technology to find the mean and the (population) standard deviation, to 3 s.f.
Mohammed writes f(g(x)) = (x + 9)(x²) for f(x) = x² and g(x) = x + 9. Explain the error.
items.answer: f(g(x)) means substitute g(x) into f: f(x + 9) = (x + 9)², not a product of f and g.
items.markingKey: Meaning of composition (R1); correct result (A1).

items.stem: "If two ships have the same speed they have the same velocity." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: They also need the same direction.
items.markingKey: They also need the same direction. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A hospital in Kuala Lumpur uses a medical isotope with a half-life of 8 hours. A dose starts at 128 mg. (a) Write a formula for the mass M after t hours. (b) Find the mass after 16 hours. (c) Without a calculator, find when the mass is 32 mg. (d) Explain whether the mass ever reaches zero.
items.answer: (a) M = 128 × (1/2)^(t/8) (b) 32 mg (c) 32 = 128 × 2^(−2), so t = 16 hours (d) it never reaches 0 exactly, because (1/2)^(t/8) > 0
items.markingKey: (a) M = 128 × (1/2)^(t/8) (b) 32 mg (c) 32 = 128 × 2^(−2), so t = 16 hours (d) it never reaches 0 exactly, because (1/2)^(t/8) > 0. Model or common base set up (M1); exponents equated and solved (A1 A1); pattern generalised (B: R1); interpretation in context (D: R1).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why starting to save earlier makes a large difference with compound interest.
items.answer: Early deposits have more years to earn interest on interest, so they grow by a larger factor. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Early deposits have more years to earn interest on interest, so they grow by a larger factor. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (4 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: The roof truss of a house in Melbourne is a triangle with base 12 m and rafters 7.7 m and 8.1 m. (a) Find the angle at the top. (b) Is it acute or obtuse? (c) Find the height of the top above the base. (d) Explain a condition the rafter lengths must satisfy.
items.answer: (a) 98.8° (b) obtuse (c) height ≈ 5.14 m (d) the rafters must fit the span: 7.7 + 8.1 > 12
items.markingKey: (a) 98.8° (b) obtuse (c) height ≈ 5.14 m (d) the rafters must fit the span: 7.7 + 8.1 > 12. Cosine rule set up (M1 A1); results accurate (A1); interpreted in context (D: R1); clear communication with units (C1).

items.stem: State the domain and range of f(x) = √(x − 3) + 8.
items.answer: domain x ≥ 3; range f(x) ≥ 8
items.markingKey: Domain x ≥ 3 (A1) – root argument ≥ 0; range f(x) ≥ 8 (A1).

items.stem: The mean monthly temperature in Mumbai ranges from 12 °C in January (t = 1) to 24 °C in July (t = 7). (a) Find the amplitude and principal axis. (b) Find b (degrees per month). (c) Write a model using cosine. (d) Use it to estimate the temperature in month 3.
items.markingKey: (a) a = 6, d = 18 (b) b = 30 (c) T = −6 cos(30(t − 1)) + 18 (d) month 3: 15.0 °C. Parameters found from the context (A1 A1); model written (M1); used to answer the question (A1); limitations discussed (D: R1).

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the points where the line y = 2x − 6 meets the curve y = x² − 5x.
items.markingKey: x² − 5x = 2x − 6 → x² − 7x + 6 = 0 (M1); x = 1, 6 (A1); y-values from the line (A1).

items.stem: Results of a survey in Dubai: adults: bus 12, bike 8, walk 6; children: bus 24, bike 22, walk 23. (a) Find the row, column and overall totals needed. (b) Find P(bus | adults) and P(bus | children). (c) Find P(bus). (d) Decide whether choosing bus is independent of the group, and explain.
items.answer: (a) totals: adults 26, children 69, bus 36, overall 95 (b) P(bus | adults) = 6/13 ≈ 0.462; P(bus | children) = 8/23 ≈ 0.348 (c) P(bus) = 36/95 ≈ 0.379 (d) not independent – the choice depends on the group

items.stem: In Dubai, the number of people at a concert was estimated as 1,000. The exact value was 1,067. Find the percentage error, correct to 2 decimal places.

Rafael invests RM5,000 in Kuala Lumpur at 6% per year compound interest. (a) Write an equation for when the investment reaches RM7,500. (b) Solve it using logarithms. (c) State the number of whole years needed. (d) Explain why the answer is the same for any starting amount.
items.answer: (a) RM5,000 × 1.06ᵗ = RM7,500 (b) t = log 1.5/log 1.06 ≈ 6.96 (c) 7 whole years (d) the time does not depend on P
